title: The Best Tryouts
premise: Isandro Crane, seventeen and the eldest of three, has spent fifteen years keeping their family's struggles invisible—until a college essay prompt asks applicants to describe 'the truth you've never said out loud.' Their draft accidentally gets shared with their best friend Priya, who recognizes Isandro's carefully hidden life in every line, forcing a reckoning about years of small lies. As scholarship deadlines collide with Mom's collapsing night shifts and the younger siblings' needs, Isandro must choose between the polished, false self that could win them admission and the honest one that might cost everything. In the end, submitting the true essay—messy, exposing, real—loses them the safe friendship but wins an unexpected admission, and teaches the whole Crane family that belonging built on hiding was never belonging at all.
about_author: C. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former admissions reader who spent six years reading ten thousand essays about silence before writing one about being heard. They live in a rust-belt city that smells like rain on brick and write at kitchen tables, always at kitchen tables.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In AP English, Ms. Okafor unveils the Common App prompt: 'the truth you've never said out loud.' Isandro writes three safe sentences about soccer, then one dangerous sentence they immediately delete—but not before it lodges under their skin. Emotional beat: the first crack in fifteen years of carefulness.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A catalog of Isandro's daily deceptions: free-lunch forms hidden, thrift-store tags cut out, little sister Marisol coached to say 'Dad travels.' The chapter establishes what invisibility costs in labor. Emotional beat: exhaustion disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Priya Knows the Version With Braces
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Best friend Priya narrates eight years of friendship from her side—the sleepovers Isandro never reciprocated, the birthday parties declined. She loves Isandro but senses the walls. Emotional beat: affection shadowed by the ache of being kept out.

chapters.title: Night Shift Math
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Mom's hospital schedule collapses; Isandro does the arithmetic of cereal boxes and bus fare while Marisol, nine, pretends to be asleep so she won't be a burden. Emotional beat: love expressed as logistics, tenderness inside scarcity.

chapters.title: The Draft That Wouldn't Stay Deleted
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At 2 a.m., Isandro writes the real essay in one unguarded rush—Dad's departure, the shame, the fear of wanting things. They save it to the shared college folder by accident and don't notice. Emotional beat: relief followed instantly by dread the reader sees coming.

chapters.title: Shared With: Priya Raman
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya opens the folder to compare deadlines and reads the essay. Every hidden thing clicks into place—the lies she'd half-forgiven reframe as protection. She doesn't know whether to feel betrayed or heartbroken for him. Emotional beat: the ground tilting.

chapters.title: The Conversation We Keep Not Having
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Two days of excruciating normalcy—lunches where neither mentions the essay, texts left on read. Finally Priya says 'I read it' and Isandro says nothing at all. Emotional beat: silence as both shield and weapon.

chapters.title: Marisol's Science Fair
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro skips a crucial counselor meeting to build Marisol's volcano project, missing the scholarship advisor's only open slot. Responsibility wins again; resentment grows teeth. Emotional beat: sacrifice curdling into quiet fury.

chapters.title: What Priya Saw in the Lines
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Isandro privately: not angry about poverty, but about being managed for years—fed a curated version of a best friend. 'You let me defend you against rumors that were true.' Emotional beat: betrayal articulated with precision.

chapters.title: The Safe Essay
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Counselor Delgado reads Isandro's polished, lie-free draft and calls it 'impressive' in a tone that means forgettable. He asks what the essay is hiding. Isandro insists: nothing. Emotional beat: the horror of succeeding at being invisible.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Mom's POV (first time). Rosa Crane, drained from a double shift, finds Isandro asleep over the laptop, essay glowing on screen. She reads it standing up in the dark. She doesn't wake him; she cries in the bathroom so the kids won't hear. Emotional beat: a mother learning her child's secret grief.

chapters.title: Deadline Weather
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Ten days to the early deadline. Priya has stopped sitting at their lunch table; the friend group takes sides without knowing why. Isandro drafts two essays side by side: the safe one and the true one. Emotional beat: paralysis between selves.

chapters.title: The Little Brother Notices Everything
chapters.summary: Teo's POV (first time). Twelve-year-old Teo, who worships Isandro, reveals he's known about the free lunches for years—he's been quietly proud, not ashamed. 'You think we're your secret. We're not.' Emotional beat: inheritance reframed; the siblings were never fooled.

chapters.title: Rumors, Cheap and Fast
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A classmate glimpses Isandro's food-stamp card at the corner store; gossip spreads. Priya defends Isandro reflexively, then realizes she's doing exactly what she resented—managing his story. Emotional beat: complicity examined.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Bus Stop
chapters.summary: Both POVs interleaved. Rain, a missed bus, and finally the full fight: Priya demands honesty, Isandro demands loyalty, each accusing the other of abandoning them first. Priya walks away. Emotional beat: the friendship breaks along the fault line of truth.

chapters.title: Rosa's Story
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Rosa finally tells Isandro about her own silenced essay—she'd won a scholarship at nineteen and gave it up when Dad left, and has spent twenty years calling it choice instead of loss. 'Careful is how I survived. It is not how I want you to live.' Emotional beat: generational inheritance named and refused.

chapters.title: Revision at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro rewrites the essay from scratch—not confessional but clear-eyed, claiming the family without apologizing for it. Marisol edits commas; Teo reads it aloud and laughs in the right places. Emotional beat: honesty becoming craft, fear becoming voice.

chapters.title: Submit
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Deadline day. Delgado warns the true essay is 'a risk.' Isandro hovers over the button, thinks of Rosa's twenty years, and submits the real one. Then throws up in the school bathroom. Emotional beat: terror and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya hears through the grapevine that Isandro submitted something raw; a mutual friend shows her a screenshot. She rereads the original accidental draft and understands it was never meant to wound her—it was meant to save him. Emotional beat: anger softening toward grief.

chapters.title: Decision Day and Other Fires
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Deferral letter arrives, then—days later—an acceptance with aid package from the reach school, citing the essay specifically. But the win feels incomplete without Priya. Emotional beat: triumph hollowed by absence.

chapters.title: The Truth Said Out Loud
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. Priya comes to the Cranes' kitchen table, uninvited, and says her piece: hurt, yes, but also 'you never once asked if I could handle your real life.' Isandro apologizes—for the lying, not the living. Emotional beat: reconciliation earned, not granted; the friendship rebuilt on new terms.

chapters.title: Belonging, Revised
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, Isandro's POV framing. Summer: Mom takes a day-shift certification course, Teo joins debate, Marisol stops pretending to sleep. Isandro reads their accepted essay aloud at the dinner table and nobody flinches. Final image: the family photo finally taken on purpose, everyone visible. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed—from silence to story.
